title: Chakra linter rules
description: Syntax of rules.toml: one [[rule]] table per check.

x-placeholders.$comment: Master list of message placeholders. Each key is a {name} that a message may use; the value says what the check substitutes. linter.py may supply only these names; tests/linter/test_rules_toml.py enforces it.
x-placeholders.count: Number of items the finding covers, such as nodes, dependencies or attributes. Rendered with thousands separators.
x-placeholders.total: Population size that count is drawn from, such as all nodes, replayable operators or GPU compute nodes. Rendered with thousands separators.
x-placeholders.error: Text of the exception that the protobuf decoder raised.
x-placeholders.type: Numeric node type that the installed Chakra schema does not define.
x-placeholders.version: Version of the installed mlc-chakra package.
x-placeholders.field: Dependency field that holds the cycle: ctrl_deps or data_deps.
x-placeholders.stream: Default stream ID (0) that all collectives use.
x-placeholders.family: Operator or kernel family name, derived from the node name and truncated for display.
x-placeholders.schema: Number of compute nodes that carry an op_schema.
x-placeholders.name: Name of the node or metadata attribute that is absent.
x-placeholders.start: Value of the start_ts metadata attribute.
x-placeholders.finish: Value of the finish_ts metadata attribute.

rule.$comment: Unique id and name across rules cannot be expressed in JSON Schema; enforced by tests/linter/test_rules_toml.py and load_rules in linter.py.

id.description: Stable code, letters plus three digits, never reused.

description.description: What the rule checks and why it matters.

severity.description: How a finding of the rule reports: fatal stops the scan, error, warning and info show the message, pass shows nothing. A check may override it per finding.

message.description: Report text; {placeholders} come from the x-placeholders master list and are limited per rule by linter.py.

exempt.description: Shell-style name patterns exempt from the check (OPS001).

consumer_impact.description: Impact the rule sets per consumer when a finding reports at fatal, error or warning; READY means no effect, as for info and pass. One impact value per consumer; a case that differs is a separate rule. READY: no known gap, the trace fully serves the consumer. LIMITED: a known gap lowers fidelity, the consumer still works. REVIEW: the linter cannot decide, manual inspection is required. NOT SUITABLE: the consumer cannot use the trace.

replay.description: Impact for replay: re-executing the recorded operators on hardware.

simulator.description: Impact for the simulator: modeling execution time from the graph.

analysis.description: Impact for analysis: studying the timing and structure of a captured run.

check.description: Integrity check that a finding of the rule fails; any such finding makes the trace fail integrity and every consumer NOT SUITABLE. Exclusive with group.

group.description: Evidence group that a finding of the rule lowers; needs level. Exclusive with check.

level.description: Level that a finding of the rule sets for its group, such as PARTIAL or ABSENT; needs group.

remediation.description: Next step that closes a finding of the rule; overrides the shared step of its group and level. Required when the rule has no group.

consumer.$comment: Per-consumer identity and text; each rule's consumer_impact line sets its impact.

remediation.$comment: Shared next steps. A check key serves an integrity check; a group and level key serves a gap. Uniqueness and coverage are enforced by load_rules in rule_config.py.
